```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5, message = FALSE)
has_quantreg <- requireNamespace("quantreg", quietly = TRUE)
has_patchwork <- requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)
has_imputation <- requireNamespace("mice", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly = TRUE)
```

This vignette covers the extended analyses of allostaticR. All data are
synthetic; coefficients of variation below are illustrative, not sourced
clinical values.

```{r data}
library(allostaticR)
reference_data <- simulate_biomarkers(1500, seed = 1, covariates = TRUE)
study <- simulate_biomarkers(400, seed = 2, covariates = TRUE)
biomarkers <- list(
  define_biomarker("sbp", "cardiovascular", "high", "mmHg", label = "Systolic BP"),
  define_biomarker("hdl", "metabolic", "low", "mg/dL", label = "HDL cholesterol"),
  define_biomarker("crp", "inflammatory", "high", "mg/L", label = "CRP", transform = "log")
)
```

## Normative references by sex and age

Allostatic load rises mechanically with age when one sample-wide quantile
is used. A protocol can instead fit thresholds within strata and as smooth
functions of age, like growth-chart centiles: quantile regression on a natural
spline of age for count methods, or age-specific means and SDs (Altman's
absolute-residual method) for z-scores. Ages outside the reference range are
not extrapolated unless the protocol allows it.

```{r centiles, eval = has_quantreg, fig.height = 7}
normative <- define_protocol(biomarkers, strata = "sex", age = "age")
reference <- fit_reference(reference_data, normative, label = "Synthetic reference")
reference_cutoffs(reference, at = data.frame(sex = "Female", age = c(30, 50, 70)))
result <- score_load(study, reference, id = "id", group = "group")
plot_centiles(result)
```

Sex-specific supplied cutoffs use named values:

```{r sex-cutoffs}
clinical <- define_protocol(list(
  define_biomarker("sbp", "cardiovascular", "high", "mmHg", cutoff = 130),
  define_biomarker("hdl", "metabolic", "low", "mg/dL", cutoff = c(Female = 50, Male = 40))
), method = "cutoff_count", strata = "sex")
reference_cutoffs(fit_reference(spec = clinical))
```

## z-scores and system balance

`method = "z_mean"` averages risk-oriented z-scores (positive towards risk)
against the reference mean and SD; `balance = "system"` gives each
physiological system equal weight.

```{r zscores}
z_spec <- define_protocol(biomarkers, method = "z_mean", balance = "system")
z_result <- score_load(study, fit_reference(reference_data, z_spec), group = "group")
summary(z_result)
```

## Why do groups differ?

With complete panels every score is a weighted sum of biomarker
contributions, so a difference in mean load splits exactly into biomarker or
system contributions.

```{r decomposition}
pooled <- score_load(study, fit_reference(reference_data, define_protocol(biomarkers)), group = "sex")
gap <- decompose_gap(pooled, B = 300)
gap
gap$plots$waterfall
```

## Risk patterns behind the score

```{r patterns, fig.height = 6}
patterns <- risk_patterns(pooled)
patterns$patterns
patterns$redundancy$meff
if (has_patchwork) patterns$plots$patterns else patterns$plots$frequency
```

```{r risk-map, eval = has_patchwork, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
plot_risk_map(pooled)
```

## Uncertainty from biological variation

Coefficients of variation must be supplied with their source, for example
from the EFLM Biological Variation Database.

```{r uncertainty}
cv <- data.frame(biomarker = c("sbp", "hdl", "crp"), cv_analytical = c(0.02, 0.02, 0.05),
  cv_within = c(0.08, 0.07, 0.40), source = "Illustrative values for this vignette")
u <- measurement_uncertainty(pooled, cv)
u$summary
u$plots$reclassification
```

`visit_changes(trajectory, variation = cv)` classifies first-to-last risk
changes with reference change values.

## Multiverse of scoring choices

```{r multiverse, eval = has_quantreg}
grid <- multiverse_grid(define_protocol(biomarkers), reference = c("pooled", "stratified", "age"),
  strata = "sex", age = "age")
multiverse <- multiverse_analysis(study, reference_data, grid, id = "id")
multiverse
multiverse$plots$stability
```

## Explicit multiple imputation

Imputation is never automatic. `impute_biomarkers()` records every imputed
cell; `score_imputed()` pools results with Rubin's rules; and
`check_imputation()` compares methods on masked observed values.

```{r imputation, eval = has_imputation}
incomplete <- study
set.seed(3)
incomplete$crp[sample.int(nrow(incomplete), 40)] <- NA
spec <- define_protocol(biomarkers)
ref <- fit_reference(reference_data, spec)
imputed <- impute_biomarkers(incomplete, spec, method = "rf", m = 5, maxit = 5, predictors = c("age", "sex"))
score_imputed(imputed, ref, group = "sex")$pooled
```
